markdown_report:
**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Existing margins measure discrimination against loader negatives. They cannot establish next-choice usefulness or validation HR@10. (2) Feedback distinguishes recent repeated interests from incidental interactions. This motivates controlled history perturbations, without treating interactions as evidence of ownership or satisfied demand. (3) The compatibility interface exposes sequence features and candidate scores. It therefore permits architecture-independent behavioral probes while preserving the trained model.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Does It Look Sequential?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) motivates shuffling to examine sequential dependence. Last-item-fixed shuffling can further separate final-event dependence from earlier ordering. (2) [Measuring Recency Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions that stronger recency is not automatically beneficial. Recent-only and recent-removed histories should therefore be compared symmetrically. (3) [Guo et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) motivate spectral embedding diagnostics. Effective rank complements mean cosine but does not establish ranking quality.

**Directions and framework.** Organize diagnostics along three axes: history dependence, representation geometry, and evidence sufficiency. Map each to an intervention, observable, and limitation: history edits → candidate-rank changes → dependence without causal intent; embedding spectrum → effective rank → geometry without quality; title/description audit → supported/unknown judgments → incomplete compatibility evidence. This separates measurable model behavior from unavailable user traits.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched history-edit probe: 5/8/3.** Originality: combines established perturbations with matched controls, but introduces no new model class. Potential: can distinguish competing explanations for failures, but sensitivity need not predict improvement. Difficulty: uses existing hooks, although constructing fair controls requires care. References: the two history studies above.
- **Spectrum-plus-margin monitor: 3/6/2.** Originality: combines complementary measurements, but largely implements established diagnostics. Potential: cheaply identifies geometric degeneration, but offers limited guidance about specific next choices. Difficulty: needs only bounded SVD and scoring, although interpretation depends on conventions. Reference: Guo et al.
- **Evidence-supported complement audit: 5/7/6.** Originality: joins explicit compatibility evidence with history anchors, but adapts existing complement reasoning. Potential: directly examines reported failure modes, but missing descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: a small audit is feasible, although reliable annotation is labor intensive. Reference: [ECCR](https://www.amazon.science/publications/eccr-explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models).

**Selected idea: matched history-edit probe.** At 0% progress, prioritize this inexpensive diagnostic before changing architecture. On fixed training-history prefixes, compare recent-suffix removal, old-interaction removal, full shuffling, and last-item-fixed shuffling. Match deletion counts; for repeated-interest deletion, additionally match control ages using title/description-derived groups. Use compacted histories consistently and retain identical unseen candidates across paired conditions.

Cache original and perturbed scores; report top-10 overlap, rank displacement, and score-scale-invariant pairwise ordering flips, with denominators and per-category summaries. Restore model mode afterward. These measurements describe dependence, not compatibility or purchase saturation. Preserve the adapter contract and choose any subsequent trained variant solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; no improvement is claimed before evaluation.

idea.description: Implement a matched history-edit diagnostic adapter that measures how recommendations depend on recency, earlier ordering, and repeated semantic interests while preserving DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader).
idea.motivation: The supplied feedback suggests that broad associations can displace specific recent interests. Existing positive-negative margins cannot distinguish these explanations. Paired interventions provide inexpensive evidence about which history signals actually affect rankings without inventing ownership, satisfaction, compatibility, or personality labels.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only public training histories and available titles/descriptions/timestamps. Select a deterministic bounded panel with equal category representation, and reuse a fixed unseen-item candidate set within each paired comparison. Separate this diagnostic panel from the pinned validation evaluator. Define repeated-interest groups through deterministic TF-IDF similarity with documented thresholds; report unavailable metadata and unmatched controls explicitly. Match repeated-interest controls on deletion count and age bins; report inability to match rather than silently relaxing criteria. Compact every deletion variant and left-pad consistently. Aggregate paired rank changes within category and then average categories equally. Retain existing margin metrics with their sampling limitations, and leave unavailable item-category breakdowns empty. Return metrics and metric_definitions, including sample sizes, intervention definitions, and missing-data rates. Use view.model to save and restore training mode in a finally block, and route scoring through the compatibility hooks. No architecture or predictor change is required for this diagnostic-only proposal. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, original splits and seeds, and trial-local artifacts. Budget all diagnostic inference against the shared search allowance.

originality.positive: Combines matched deletion controls, last-item-fixed shuffling, and semantic repetition interventions under one architecture-compatible interface.
originality.negative: History perturbations and rank-sensitivity measurements already have direct precedents; novelty lies mainly in experimental control and integration.

future_potential.positive: Creates falsifiable evidence for deciding whether later changes should address recency, ordering, or repeated-interest aggregation.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may not predict validation gains, and observational histories cannot identify true intent or fulfilled needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing feature and scoring hooks support implementation without retraining or changing the predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Matched controls, metadata coverage, padding conventions, and consistent scoring require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: Uses history shuffling to investigate the strength of sequential structure, motivating paired ordering interventions.
limitations: Shuffling sensitivity alone does not establish user intent or identify an improved recommendation model.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: Reports that excessive recent-history emphasis can hurt accuracy, motivating symmetric recency probes.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal recency policy for the four specified Amazon categories.

related_work.title: Guo et al., ICML 2024: recommendation embedding collapse
contributions: Studies embedding collapse and constraints on representation dimensionality, motivating spectral diagnostics.
limitations: Embedding geometry alone does not establish recommendation quality or explain compatibility failures.

related_work.title: ECCR: Explainable and Coherent Complement Recommendation Based on Large Language Models
contributions: Treats coherent complements as requiring compatibility and relevance, motivating explicit evidence checks.
limitations: The supplied task lacks reliable ownership and prerequisite labels; missing evidence must remain unknown.
